units.source_text: 且说明石皇后为叔父式部卿亲王服轻丧，这期间还住在六条院。

en.t: Now Empress Akashi was observing light mourning for her uncle, Prince Shikibukyo, and during that time she was still living at Rokujo-in.

units.source_text: 匂亲王的哥哥二皇子代任了式部卿，这官位很尊严，不能常来参谒母后。

en.t: Niou's elder brother, the Second Prince, had taken over the office of Shikibukyo, and since this was a very dignified post, he could not often come to pay respects to their mother.

units.source_text: 匂亲王心绪不佳，寂寞无聊，常到与母后同来的姐姐大公主那里去闲玩，借以散心。

en.t: Niou was in low spirits, lonely and bored, so he often went to idle away time with his elder sister, the First Princess, who had come with their mother, in order to distract himself.

units.source_text: 大公主身边美貌侍女甚多，匂亲王未得仔细欣赏，引以为憾。

en.t: There were many beautiful ladies-in-waiting around the First Princess, and Niou regretted that he had not yet had a chance to admire them closely.

units.source_text: 薰大将也不禁动情，偷偷地爱上了大公主身边的侍女小宰相君，其人相貌也很漂亮。

en.t: General Kaoru too could not help being moved, and secretly fell in love with Kozaisho no Kimi, a lady-in-waiting beside the First Princess, who was also very beautiful.

units.source_text: 薰大将认为这是一个品性优越的女子。

en.t: General Kaoru considered her a woman of superior character.

units.source_text: 同是弹琴或弹琵琶，她的爪音、拨音比别人美妙。

en.t: Whether she played the koto or the biwa, the sound of her fingernails and plectrum was more exquisite than anyone else's.

units.source_text: 写信或讲话，也往往添加富有情趣的词句。

en.t: When writing letters or speaking, she also often added words and phrases full of feeling and charm.

units.source_text: 匂亲王以前也认为这是一个美人，照例企图破坏薰大将对她的恋情而据为己有。

en.t: Niou had also long thought her a beauty, and, as usual, tried to disrupt General Kaoru's love for her and take her for himself.

units.source_text: 但小宰相君说：“我为什么要像别人那样服从他！”

en.t: But Kozaisho no Kimi said, Why should I obey him the way other women do!

units.source_text: 严肃的薰大将就相信“此人异于常人”。

en.t: The serious General Kaoru therefore became convinced that she was different from ordinary people.

units.source_text: 小宰相君察知薰大将心甚悲伤，不忍坐视，赋诗奉呈，诗曰：

en.t: Kozaisho no Kimi sensed that General Kaoru's heart was deeply sorrowful and could not bear to look on in silence, so she composed a poem and presented it to him. The poem said:
